newsitem.title: LEBANON: Press watchdog asks Lebanon to free journalist.
newsitem.headline: Press watchdog asks Lebanon to free journalist.

text.p: A Paris-based group that defends press freedom urged Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri on Tuesday to release a Lebanese journalist arrested during a recent detention campaign against opposition members in Lebanon.

Christian journalist Pierre Atallah of the Beirut conservative An-Nahar newspaper was detained by "the Lebanese army and army intelligence" on Monday night, Joubran Tweini, one of the owners of An-Nahar, told Reuters.

"Reporters sans Frontieres asks you to use your influence to intervene so that either specific charges are pressed against Pierre Atallah or that he is immediately released if the arrest is linked to his journalistic activity or political opinions," the group said in a letter to Hariri, a copy of which was faxed to an international news organisation in Beirut.
When asked to comment on the report, a senior security official told Reuters "all detentions are of a security nature and not related to the freedom of expression".
"They are carried out under the supervision of specialised judicial authorities," the source said.
Recent detentions were sparked by an incident last week in which a van carrying Syrian workers was machine-gunned in a predominantly Christian area, killing the driver and injuring some passengers.
The RSF said Atallah was detained shortly before midnight by "military intelligence agents and the army" without arrest warrants.

Tweini said: "Pierre was kidnapped, not detained. The two men who came after him, an army officer and an army intelligence agent, refused to show him any arrest warrant. They pointed their guns at his head and took him to an unknown place.
"Our lawyer (of the daily) MP Boutros Harb learned today that Pierre is held at the defence ministry," Tweini added.
Defence ministry officials declined to comment on the issue.
Prosecutor-General Adnan Addoum said on Monday 26 people out of 48 people detained in the campaign were freed. None of the remaining detainees had yet been charged with any offences, he said.
Lebanese Christian opposition politicians at home and in Paris put the number of detainees at 200.
Beirut newspapers quoted President Elias Hrawi on Tuesday as accusing Israel of supporting agents to destabilise the country.
"Only very few people who are still moved by Israel and others are still trying to obstruct internal peace," Hrawi was quoted as saying.
Syria has 35,000 troops in Lebanon and is the country's main power broker.
